summary: Google requires a Cloud project and OAuth consent screen configuration for all apps. Developers must separate testing and production environments, verify domains, and submit apps using sensitive scopes for verification. Production apps require a public home page with specific legal policies.

claim.text: All apps using OAuth 2.0 require a consent screen configuration.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: All apps using OAuth 2.0 require a consent screen configuration, but you only need to list scopes for apps used by people outside your Google Workspace organization.

claim.text: You must obtain OAuth 2.0 client credentials from the Google API Console.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: To begin, obtain OAuth 2.0 client credentials from the Google API Console.

claim.text: Google requires separate projects for testing and production environments.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Google's OAuth policies require separate projects for testing and production.

claim.text: Production apps must have a publicly accessible home page.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Every production app that uses OAuth 2.0 must have a publicly accessible home page.

claim.text: The home page must include a description, privacy policy, and terms of service.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Your application's home page must include a description of the app's functionality, as well as links to a privacy policy and optional terms of service.

claim.text: All domains associated with the app must be verified.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Google's OAuth consent screen verification process requires verification of all domains associated with your project's home page, privacy policy, terms of service, authorized redirect URIs, or authorized JavaScript origins.

claim.text: Apps using sensitive or restricted scopes must be submitted for verification.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: If your production app uses sensitive or restricted scopes, you must submit your use of those scopes for verification before you include the scopes in an authorization request.

claim.text: Apps require verification if they are configured for external users and display a logo or display name on the OAuth consent screen.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Your app requires verification if configured for external users and displays a logo or display name on the OAuth consent screen.

claim.text: Apps in the Testing status have a 7-day refresh token expiration limit.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: This status overrides certain standard OAuth limitations for the organization's users, such as the 100-test-user cap and the 7-day refresh token expiration limit for apps in the Testing status.

claim.text: Apps in the Testing status are limited to a hard cap of 100 test users.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Only users explicitly added to the test user allowlist can access the app (limited to a hard cap of 100 test users).

claim.text: Published unverified apps requesting sensitive or restricted scopes are limited to a hard cap of 100 total users.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Additionally, for apps requesting sensitive or restricted scopes, unverified app warnings (Danger UI) will be displayed to users, and a hard cap of 100 total users applies.

claim.text: Security assessments must be completed at least every 12 months.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: As mentioned previously, to keep access to any verified restricted scopes, apps must be reverified for compliance and complete a security assessment at least every 12 months after your assessor's Letter of Assessment (LOA) approval date.
